newsitem.title: UK: Brazil 96/97 sugar output seen at 13.8 mln T -Man.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 96/97 sugar output seen at 13.8 mln T -Man.

text.p: Brazil's sugar production in 1996/97 should amount to 13.8 million tonnes tel quel, 600,000 tonnes higher than in the previous year, E D & F Man said on Tuesday.

In its latest monthly report, Man said output in the centre-south region had overtaken last year's final figure of 9.83 million tonnes to reach 10.36 million and final output was likely to be close to this figure as most mills had completed crushing.
Centre-south production is therefore expected to fall short of the authorised figure of 10.47 million tonnes, it said.
In the north north-east region, final sugar production was expected to come in at around the same level as last year, or 3.4 million tonnes.
Man said the extra authorised export quota -- an increase of 552,318 tonnes to bring the total to 5.75 million tonnes -- was unlikely to be used up by mills.
These might opt instead to carry over their authorisations to the next crop, it said.
"Furthermore, this additional quantity is still subject to the 40 percent export tax though the government is set to remove this in the near future," the report said.
